Black Shuck.alt: A huge black dog crossing a rain-soaked lane near a medieval Norfolk church
Black Shuck.caption: A visual interpretation of the East Anglian legend
Black Shuck.pullquote: To meet his gaze, tradition holds, is to be marked for death within the twelvemonth.
Black Shuck.editorial: We chose to open the East Anglian black-dog tradition with Black Shuck because the 1577 Bungay account is one of the earliest dated, place-specific sightings in English folklore — a rare case where a supernatural legend is pinned to a named church, a named storm and a surviving contemporary pamphlet. The scorch marks on the door of Holy Trinity, Blythburgh are still shown to visitors today.

Lambton Worm.alt: An enormous dark serpent coiling through the shallows of the River Wear
Lambton Worm.caption: A visual interpretation of the County Durham legend
Lambton Worm.pullquote: He must then slay the first living thing he met, or a curse would fall on nine generations of Lambtons.

Barghest.alt: A large black hound standing beside an old Yorkshire churchyard
Barghest.caption: A visual interpretation of the Yorkshire legend
Barghest.pullquote: To see the Barghest, or to hear its howl, was widely held to be an omen of death.

The Loch Ness Monster.alt: A long dark creature breaking the surface of Loch Ness beneath misty Highland slopes
The Loch Ness Monster.caption: A visual interpretation of the Loch Ness legend
The Loch Ness Monster.pullquote: Modern Nessie has been hunted by cameras, submarines and sonar for over a century, always elusive.

The Green Man.alt: A weathered Green Man carving with a leaf-framed face set into the stone of a medieval Gloucestershire church
The Green Man.caption: A visual interpretation of the Gloucestershire Green Man tradition
The Green Man.pullquote: Though Christian craftsmen cut him into the bosses and capitals of medieval churches, his roots seem far older.

Kelpie.alt: A black horse-like spirit standing chest-deep at the edge of a Highland loch under heavy clouds
Kelpie.caption: A visual interpretation of the Highland kelpie tradition
Kelpie.section_heading: The horse at the water's edge
Kelpie.pullquote: The moment a rider mounts they find themselves stuck fast as the creature plunges into the deep to drown and devour them.

Banshee.alt: A solitary woman in pale dress keening on a rain-dark rural Irish lane beside stone walls at dusk
Banshee.caption: A visual interpretation of the Irish banshee tradition
Banshee.pullquote: To hear her is not to cause death, only to be warned of it.

Merlin.alt: An older bearded seer in a dark cloak sitting beside a rocky Welsh cave above a misty valley
Merlin.caption: A visual interpretation of the Merlin tradition in Wales
Merlin.pullquote: He ends ensnared by his own pupil, the Lady of the Lake, sealed forever in a cave or a tree: the seer who foresaw all things but his own fall.

Y Ddraig Goch.alt: A red dragon and a pale white dragon confronting each other among the misty ruins and rocky slopes of Dinas Emrys
Y Ddraig Goch.caption: A visual interpretation of the Welsh red dragon prophecy
Y Ddraig Goch.pullquote: The young Merlin prophesied that the red dragon — the true Britons — would ultimately prevail.

The Dullahan.alt: A headless rider on a black horse carrying a severed head that glows like a lantern on a dark Irish lane
The Dullahan.caption: A visual interpretation of the Irish Dullahan tradition
The Dullahan.pullquote: A headless horseman carrying his own severed head, which glows like a lantern.

Cailleach.alt: An ancient one-eyed woman wrapped in dark wool standing among boulders on a stormy Highland mountainside
Cailleach.caption: A visual interpretation of the Highland Cailleach tradition
Cailleach.pullquote: With her hammer and creel she shapes the land itself, letting boulders fall to raise mountains and carve out glens.

The Morrigan.alt: A dark-cloaked woman standing in a shallow Irish ford beneath storm clouds with a crow wheeling nearby
The Morrigan.caption: A visual interpretation of the Irish Morrigan tradition
The Morrigan.pullquote: She is both: a sovereign goddess of the land, a prophetess of battle-death, and a figure whose presence on the margins of a fight means the fight has already been decided.

The Dagda.alt: A huge weathered man beside an iron cauldron, old harp and wooden club near an earthen mound in County Meath
The Dagda.caption: A visual interpretation of the Dagda in Irish mythology
The Dagda.pullquote: These are the tools of a god who controls death, abundance, and time.

King Arthur.alt: A weathered British war-leader with a sword and dark horse standing to the right of misty Glastonbury Tor
King Arthur.caption: A visual interpretation of King Arthur in the Somerset landscape
King Arthur.pullquote: Tradition holds that Arthur never truly died but sleeps beneath a hill with his knights, ready to return in Britain's hour of greatest need.

Avalon.alt: A small wooden boat carrying a wounded cloaked figure toward a misty island across the flooded Somerset Levels
Avalon.caption: A visual interpretation of Arthur's journey to Avalon
Avalon.pullquote: Arthur sleeps here still, waiting to return when Britain needs him most.

Robin Hood.alt: A weathered medieval archer standing beside a massive oak in the shadowed depths of Sherwood Forest
Robin Hood.caption: A visual interpretation of Robin Hood in Sherwood Forest
Robin Hood.pullquote: The core of the legend is simple and endlessly renewable: a skilled archer, living under the greenwood of Sherwood Forest.

Stonehenge.alt: The weathered stones of Stonehenge standing on Salisbury Plain as pale midsummer light breaks through mist
Stonehenge.caption: A visual interpretation of Stonehenge at midsummer dawn
Stonehenge.pullquote: Raised by giants according to Geoffrey of Monmouth, or conjured by Merlin from Ireland.

The Green Knight.alt: A towering green knight in dark plate and mail entering Arthur's winter hall with an iron axe and holly branch
The Green Knight.caption: A visual interpretation of the Green Knight's challenge at Arthur's court
The Green Knight.pullquote: His beheading game with Gawain tests courage, courtesy, truth, and the strangeness of winter.

Beowulf.alt: An unarmed early medieval warrior facing a huge shadowed figure inside the dark timber hall of Heorot
Beowulf.caption: A visual interpretation of Beowulf awaiting Grendel in Heorot
Beowulf.pullquote: Beowulf waits in the darkened hall and fights Grendel bare-handed.

Fionn mac Cumhaill.alt: Young Fionn tasting his burned thumb beside a salmon cooking over a small fire on a wooded Irish riverbank
Fionn mac Cumhaill.caption: A visual interpretation of Fionn gaining wisdom from the Salmon of Knowledge
Fionn mac Cumhaill.pullquote: Fionn got it all by accident, and ever after could access that wisdom by sucking his thumb.

The Wild Hunt.alt: Spectral medieval riders and howling hounds sweeping through rain across a moonlit North Yorkshire moor
The Wild Hunt.caption: A visual interpretation of the Wild Hunt over the Yorkshire moors
The Wild Hunt.pullquote: To witness the Hunt is to receive a portent of war, plague, or the death of a king.

Giant's Causeway.alt: Fionn mac Cumhaill watching a far larger giant approach across the wet basalt columns of the Antrim coast
Giant's Causeway.caption: A visual interpretation of Fionn and Benandonner at the Giant's Causeway
Giant's Causeway.pullquote: Reasoning that if the infant was this size, its father must be a giant beyond anything he could survive, Benandonner fled.

Cú Chulainn.alt: Cú Chulainn standing alone with spear and shield in a rain-dark Irish river ford as an army waits beyond
Cú Chulainn.caption: A visual interpretation of Cú Chulainn holding the ford
Cú Chulainn.pullquote: He holds the ford alone, fighting single combats by day and recovering by night.

Selkies of Orkney.alt: A woman kneeling beside a grey seal skin on a cold Orkney shore while a seal watches from the shallows
Selkies of Orkney.caption: A visual interpretation of the selkie tradition in Orkney
Selkies of Orkney.pullquote: If a fisherman steals a selkie's skin, she cannot return to the sea and must live as his wife — yearning always for the ocean.

Herne the Hunter.alt: A horned spectral huntsman dissolving into mist and leaves as phantom hounds and riders cross Windsor Great Park
Herne the Hunter.caption: A visual interpretation of Herne the Hunter and his phantom hunt
Herne the Hunter.pullquote: He now haunts it as a ghost with great ragged horns, blasting the trees and taking cattle.

Nuckelavee.alt: A skinless horse demon fused with a long-armed human torso emerging from the stormy sea on an Orkney shore
Nuckelavee.caption: A visual interpretation of the dreaded Orcadian Nuckelavee
Nuckelavee.pullquote: Its very breath blighted crops, sickened livestock and brought the wasting epidemic the islanders called mortasheen.

Brownie.alt: A small shaggy household spirit with oversized hands working a wooden churn beside a Scottish farmhouse hearth
Brownie.caption: A visual interpretation of the Scottish Brownie at its night work
Brownie.pullquote: He asks no wage, only a bowl of cream or a fresh bannock left quietly by the hearth.

Redcap.alt: A squat red-eyed goblin with iron claws and boots crouching inside a rain-dark ruined Scottish border tower
Redcap.caption: A visual interpretation of the murderous Redcap of the Scottish Borders
Redcap.section_heading: The goblin in the ruined keep
Redcap.pullquote: Should the blood in his cap ever dry, he will die.

Puck.alt: An ancient horned woodland spirit with bark-like skin standing in a mossy sunken lane in the Sussex Weald
Puck.caption: A visual interpretation of Puck as an ancient spirit of the Sussex Weald
Puck.pullquote: An ancient spirit of place tied to the Sussex Weald, known since before the Normans came.

Bodach.alt: A long-limbed soot and smoke apparition descending through the chimney of a dark Highland blackhouse
Bodach.caption: A visual interpretation of the Highland Bodach entering through the chimney
Bodach.pullquote: He is not a ghost or a fairy in the usual sense but something more elemental: a presence associated with darkness, threat, and the small hours.

Each-Uisge.alt: A weed-draped grey water horse standing at the edge of a misty Highland loch in Argyll
Each-Uisge.caption: A visual interpretation of the Each-Uisge waiting beside a Highland loch
Each-Uisge.section_heading: The glamour at the water's edge
Each-Uisge.pullquote: Those who mounted it could not dismount as it plunged into the depths.

Jenny Greenteeth.alt: A green-skinned river hag with pondweed hair emerging from a still Lancashire pond
Jenny Greenteeth.caption: A visual interpretation of Jenny Greenteeth beneath a weed-covered pond
Jenny Greenteeth.pullquote: She drags the unwary - particularly children - to their deaths in the depths.

Blue Men of the Minch.alt: Blue-grey sea beings rising from Atlantic waves between the Hebridean islands as a sailing ship passes
Blue Men of the Minch.caption: A visual interpretation of the Blue Men challenging a vessel in the Minch
Blue Men of the Minch.pullquote: They challenge passing captains to a battle of rhyming verse - fail and they drag the vessel under.

Abhartach.alt: An earth-stained dwarf-magician revenant standing beside a disturbed stone burial monument in Slaghtaverty
Abhartach.caption: A visual interpretation of Abhartach returning from his burial at Slaghtaverty
Abhartach.section_heading: The magician who would not stay buried
Abhartach.pullquote: A cruel dwarf-magician who repeatedly returned after burial.

Afanc.alt: A chained amphibious lake monster with wet fur, scales and a powerful tail on a Gwynedd shore
Afanc.caption: A visual interpretation of the Afanc bound beside a Welsh mountain lake
Afanc.section_heading: The monster drawn from the lake
Afanc.pullquote: A shape-shifting water monster that haunted Welsh lakes.

Balor of the Evil Eye.alt: Four warriors straining to lift the single glowing eye of the giant Balor on a windswept Tory Island battlefield
Balor of the Evil Eye.caption: A visual interpretation of Balor's deadly eye being opened for battle
Balor of the Evil Eye.section_heading: The eye that killed all it saw
Balor of the Evil Eye.pullquote: It took four men to lift his eyelid in battle.

Aillen mac Midgna.alt: An otherworldly musician playing before sleeping defenders as Tara's timber hall burns on Samhain night
Aillen mac Midgna.caption: A visual interpretation of Aillen enchanting the defenders of Tara
Aillen mac Midgna.pullquote: Each Samhain, Aillen mac Midgna lulled the defenders of Tara to sleep with enchanted music before burning the royal hall.

Alderley Edge.alt: An old guide leading a farmer and white horse into a sandstone cavern where Arthur and his knights sleep
Alderley Edge.caption: A visual interpretation of the sleeping king beneath Alderley Edge
Alderley Edge.pullquote: Arthur and his knights sleep beneath the rock until Britain needs them.

Alice Kyteler.alt: Alice Kyteler beside herbs and a stone mortar in a medieval Kilkenny townhouse as a black dog waits in shadow
Alice Kyteler.caption: A visual interpretation of the accusations surrounding Alice Kyteler in medieval Kilkenny
Alice Kyteler.pullquote: Her own stepchildren accused her of poisoning each of her four husbands.

Blackbeard.alt: Blackbeard standing on a weathered sailing ship at dawn with smoking match cords beneath his hat
Blackbeard.caption: A visual interpretation of Blackbeard's fearsome image at sea
Blackbeard.section_heading: The pirate who became a legend
Blackbeard.pullquote: His fearsome image outgrew his short career.

facts.Legend: Buried treasure and a headless spirit

Boudicca.alt: Boudicca commanding Iceni warriors from a two-horse chariot beneath a storm-lit East Anglian sky
Boudicca.caption: A visual interpretation of Boudicca leading the revolt against Rome
Boudicca.pullquote: She united the Iceni with the Trinovantes of Essex.

Unicorn.alt: A powerful silver-grey unicorn with a broken iron chain standing in a sunlit Scottish glen
Unicorn.caption: A visual interpretation of Scotland's proud and untameable unicorn
Unicorn.section_heading: The beast too wild for kings
Unicorn.pullquote: In Scottish heraldry, the unicorn is always shown chained, because an unchained unicorn is too dangerous and too free to be trusted near a king.

Camelot.alt: A great timber hall and fortified royal settlement crowning South Cadbury hill above the Somerset landscape
Camelot.caption: A visual interpretation of Camelot as a post-Roman hillfort at South Cadbury
Camelot.pullquote: The legendary seat of Arthur's kingdom is most often identified with South Cadbury hillfort in Somerset.

Griffin.alt: A lion-bodied, eagle-headed griffin with broad feathered wings guarding treasure in a high rocky nest
Griffin.caption: A visual interpretation of the griffin as a vigilant guardian of treasure
Griffin.pullquote: A lion-bodied, eagle-headed guardian of treasure, enemy of horses, and one of the great beasts of British heraldry.

Anne Bonny.alt: Anne Bonny standing watchfully with a cutlass on the deck of an early eighteenth-century sailing ship
Anne Bonny.caption: A visual interpretation of Anne Bonny during the Golden Age of Piracy
Anne Bonny.pullquote: Sparse historical records left room for a much larger legend.

Leprechaun.alt: A small, weathered fairy shoemaker working at a leather shoe in a hidden workshop beneath a hawthorn bank
Leprechaun.caption: A visual interpretation of the solitary leprechaun at his shoemaker's bench
Leprechaun.pullquote: A solitary fairy shoemaker famous for hidden treasure and impossible bargains.

Morgan le Fay.alt: Morgan le Fay standing beside a rain-filled stone basin above the sea near Tintagel at dawn
Morgan le Fay.caption: A visual interpretation of Morgan le Fay as healer, enchantress and otherworldly protector
Morgan le Fay.section_heading: The enchantress who changes with the tale
Morgan le Fay.pullquote: Her character shifts between healer, magical adversary and Arthur's otherworldly protector.

Beast of Bodmin.alt: A large black panther-like cat moving through wet bracken beneath the granite tors of Bodmin Moor
Beast of Bodmin.caption: A visual interpretation of a Beast of Bodmin sighting at dusk
Beast of Bodmin.section_heading: The cat in the Cornish dusk
Beast of Bodmin.pullquote: Official investigations found no conclusive evidence, yet sightings persist to this day.

Kraken.alt: A colossal many-armed sea creature surfacing like an island near a sailing vessel off Orkney
Kraken.caption: A visual interpretation of the Kraken revealing itself beneath the Orkney waves
Kraken.pullquote: Norse sagas describe it as large enough to be mistaken for an island.

Lancelot.alt: Lancelot and a young squire carefully helping a wounded older knight down from a horse beside a misty lake
Lancelot.caption: A visual interpretation of Lancelot as knight, companion and rescuer
Lancelot.pullquote: The greatest knight of the Round Table and Arthur's closest companion - until love for Guinevere destroyed both.

Arawn.alt: Arawn standing with a white hunting hound in a luminous, misted Welsh Otherworld landscape
Arawn.caption: A visual interpretation of Arawn as the regal king of Annwn
Arawn.section_heading: The king beyond the mortal world
Arawn.pullquote: He is not a devil, but a ruler of another order of being.

Sir Galahad.alt: Sir Galahad in mail kneeling before a simple luminous cup in a quiet medieval chapel
Sir Galahad.caption: A visual interpretation of Galahad achieving the Holy Grail
Sir Galahad.section_heading: The knight who reached the Grail
Sir Galahad.pullquote: The only knight pure enough to achieve the Grail.

Andraste.alt: The warrior goddess Andraste appearing in an East Anglian grove before gathered Iceni fighters
Andraste.caption: A visual interpretation of Andraste invoked before Boudicca's revolt
Andraste.section_heading: The goddess at the edge of history
Andraste.pullquote: A warrior goddess invoked by Boudica before her revolt against Rome.

Baobhan Sith.alt: Three pale supernatural women in green gowns dancing near horses and an iron gate in the moonlit Highlands
Baobhan Sith.caption: A visual interpretation of the Baobhan Sith dancing in the Highland wilderness
Baobhan Sith.pullquote: Beautiful women in green gowns who appear to hunters in the wilderness, dance with them through the night, and drain their blood.

Gawain.alt: Gawain riding away from the distant Green Chapel while examining the green girdle wrapped around his hand
Gawain.caption: A visual interpretation of Gawain leaving the Green Chapel after his test
Gawain.section_heading: The knight whose honour was tested
Gawain.pullquote: His strange bargain with the Green Knight tested not his sword arm but his honour.

facts.Gift: Strength that waxed with the sun

Sir Percival.alt: Percival watching a solemn cup and spear procession pass through a candlelit medieval hall
Sir Percival.caption: A visual interpretation of Percival at the Grail castle
Sir Percival.pullquote: He was the first to reach the Grail castle - and asked the wrong question, or failed to ask any at all.

Mordred.alt: A shaved-headed Mordred seated over a campaign map with uneasy captains before Camlann
Mordred.caption: A visual interpretation of Mordred planning the campaign that ends the Round Table
Mordred.section_heading: The man who ended the Round Table
Mordred.pullquote: The one who ends the Round Table, and cannot be entirely condemned for it.

facts.Motif: The fall of the Round Table

Henry Morgan.alt: Henry Morgan studying a sea chart with sailors in a storm-cleared seventeenth-century Caribbean harbour
Henry Morgan.caption: A visual interpretation of Henry Morgan planning a Caribbean voyage
Henry Morgan.section_heading: The privateer who became a pirate legend
Henry Morgan.pullquote: Later retellings turned the historical governor and plantation owner into a larger-than-life pirate figure.

Fairy Flag of Dunvegan.alt: Clan custodians carefully unfurling an ancient silk banner in the storm-lit hall of Dunvegan Castle
Fairy Flag of Dunvegan.caption: A visual interpretation of the Fairy Flag being unfurled in a time of peril
Fairy Flag of Dunvegan.section_heading: The banner kept for the darkest hour
Fairy Flag of Dunvegan.pullquote: Clan tradition says it can be unfurled in times of peril to bring victory.

facts.Limit: Its magic can be used three times

Giant of the Wrekin.alt: A colossal giant carrying a spadeful of earth meeting a travelling cobbler on the Shropshire plain
Giant of the Wrekin.caption: A visual interpretation of the trick that created the Wrekin
Giant of the Wrekin.section_heading: The hill made by a clever lie
Giant of the Wrekin.pullquote: A spiteful Welsh giant carrying a spadeful of earth to dam the Severn was tricked into thinking Shrewsbury was too far.

facts.Motif: A giant outwitted by a cobbler

William Wallace.alt: William Wallace seen from behind directing Scottish spearmen across the narrow wooden bridge at Stirling
William Wallace.caption: A visual interpretation of Wallace commanding at Stirling Bridge
William Wallace.section_heading: The victory that became a legend
William Wallace.pullquote: Wallace defeated the English at Stirling Bridge in 1297 and became an enduring symbol of resistance.

Spring-Heeled Jack.alt: Spring-Heeled Jack breathing blue flame as he leaps between rooftops above a gaslit Victorian London street
Spring-Heeled Jack.caption: A visual interpretation of Spring-Heeled Jack escaping across the London rooftops
Spring-Heeled Jack.pullquote: He could leap over rooftops, breathe blue flame, and vanished whenever cornered.

Robert the Bruce.alt: A red-bearded Robert the Bruce seated in profile inside a sea cave, watching a spider rebuild its web
Robert the Bruce.caption: A visual interpretation of the spider inspiring Robert the Bruce
Robert the Bruce.pullquote: When the spider finally succeeded, its persistence inspired Bruce to continue his own struggle.

Brigid.alt: A cloaked woman tending a low sacred fire beside a timber church in an early Irish settlement at dawn
Brigid.caption: A visual interpretation of Brigid and the sacred flame tradition
Brigid.pullquote: Christianised as Saint Brigid, her flame was tended for centuries at Kildare.

facts.Legacy: Saint Brigid and the Kildare flame

Children of Lir.alt: Four white swans gliding across dark coastal water beneath the cliffs of County Mayo at dawn
Children of Lir.caption: A visual interpretation of the Children of Lir on the western Irish coast
Children of Lir.section_heading: The long exile on the water
Children of Lir.pullquote: Their singing was so beautiful that all who heard it forgot their sorrows.

facts.Waters: Lough Derravaragh, the Sea of Moyle and Erris

Avebury.alt: Towering standing stones at Avebury rising from misty grass with the village beyond at dawn
Avebury.caption: A visual interpretation of Avebury at dawn
Avebury.section_heading: The stones that move by night
Avebury.pullquote: At night the stones are said to move, drink from the stream, and return before dawn.

Blarney Stone.alt: A visitor leaning backwards to kiss the Blarney Stone while an attendant supports them on the castle battlements
Blarney Stone.caption: A visual interpretation of the Blarney Stone tradition at Blarney Castle
Blarney Stone.pullquote: According to legend, kissing the stone endows the kisser with the gift of the gab.

Blodeuwedd.alt: Blodeuwedd transforming from a flower-made woman into an owl among broom and meadowsweet in the Welsh mountains
Blodeuwedd.caption: A visual interpretation of Blodeuwedd's transformation in the Mabinogi
Blodeuwedd.pullquote: As punishment the wizard Gwydion turned her into an owl.

Will-o'-the-Wisp.alt: Cold blue-white lights hovering above flooded reeds as a lone traveller hesitates in the dark Cambridgeshire Fens
Will-o'-the-Wisp.caption: A visual interpretation of deceptive marsh lights in the English Fens
Will-o'-the-Wisp.pullquote: Mischievous spirits were believed to lure travellers off safe paths into treacherous bogs.

Ceridwen.alt: Ceridwen reaching across her steaming cauldron as three drops of inspiration leap toward the startled Gwion Bach
Ceridwen.caption: A visual interpretation of Gwion Bach tasting the cauldron of inspiration
Ceridwen.pullquote: When Gwion Bach accidentally tasted three drops, Ceridwen pursued him through a cycle of transformations.

Tintagel Castle.alt: The sea-cut ruins of Tintagel Castle rising above stormy Atlantic cliffs on the Cornish coast
Tintagel Castle.caption: A visual interpretation of Tintagel Castle after an Atlantic storm
Tintagel Castle.pullquote: Its sea-cut ruins keep Arthurian legend pinned to the Cornish coast.

Brown Lady of Raynham Hall.alt: A translucent brown-robed apparition descending the dark wooden staircase of a Norfolk country house
Brown Lady of Raynham Hall.caption: A visual interpretation of the Brown Lady descending the staircase at Raynham Hall
Brown Lady of Raynham Hall.pullquote: Britain's most famous ghost photograph shows a brown-robed figure descending a staircase at Raynham Hall.

Black Annis.alt: The one-eyed blue-faced Black Annis reaching iron claws toward a tiny cottage window in the Dane Hills
Black Annis.caption: A visual interpretation of Black Annis unable to reach through a Leicestershire cottage window
Black Annis.section_heading: The terror of the Dane Hills
Black Annis.pullquote: Old cottages in the district were built with deliberately small windows so that she could not reach a clawed arm inside.

Aos Sí.alt: A procession of luminous otherworldly people emerging from an ancient grass-covered mound in Ireland
Aos Sí.caption: A visual interpretation of the Aos Sí emerging from a hollow hill at twilight
Aos Sí.pullquote: To disturb their homes brings ruin. To be taken by them is to never fully return.

Am Fear Liath Mòr.alt: A mountaineer fleeing across the misty Ben Macdui plateau as a vast grey spectral figure looms behind
Am Fear Liath Mòr.caption: A visual interpretation of the Big Grey Man haunting Ben Macdui
Am Fear Liath Mòr.pullquote: Experienced mountaineers have reported crushing dread, phantom footsteps in the snow, and a looming presence that drives men from the mountain in blind terror.

Allison Balfour.alt: Allison Balfour standing resolutely with two officials on a timber platform above a wintry Orkney shore
Allison Balfour.caption: A visual interpretation of Allison Balfour publicly retracting her forced confession
Allison Balfour.pullquote: On the scaffold, before her execution, she publicly retracted everything, declaring the confession false and extracted only by torture.

facts.Accusation: Witchcraft against the Earl of Orkney

Angelystor.alt: A spectral angelic presence forming in the ancient Llangernyw yew as a lone tailor listens in the moonlit churchyard
Angelystor.caption: A visual interpretation of Angelystor speaking from the yew at St Digain's Church
Angelystor.pullquote: Each Halloween night, the spirit announces the names of parishioners who will die in the coming year.

Asrai.alt: A translucent Asrai dissolving into silver water beside a fishing boat as dawn reaches an English lake
Asrai.caption: A visual interpretation of an Asrai melting away in the first sunlight
Asrai.section_heading: The spirit that vanished at dawn
Asrai.pullquote: A delicate water spirit said to melt away if captured or exposed to sunlight.

Wulver.alt: The wolf-headed Wulver seated on a coastal rock in Shetland while pulling a fish from a handline
Wulver.caption: A visual interpretation of the gentle Wulver fishing alone in Shetland
Wulver.pullquote: The Wulver fishes alone and is said to leave food for poor families on windowsills.

Y Ladi Wen.alt: A translucent White Lady extending her hand to a hesitant traveller beside the flooded ford at Ogmore Castle
Y Ladi Wen.caption: A visual interpretation of Y Ladi Wen waiting at a threshold in the Welsh landscape
Y Ladi Wen.pullquote: Sometimes she extends a hand and asks for company on the road.

Anantis Castle Revenant.alt: A swollen shrouded revenant stalking a foggy medieval Northumbrian lane as two men watch from a doorway
Anantis Castle Revenant.caption: A visual interpretation of William of Newburgh's plague-bringing Anantis revenant
Anantis Castle Revenant.pullquote: Thereafter his corpse roamed abroad by night, and wherever it passed the air grew foul and a wasting sickness spread.

facts.Setting: Anantis castle, often linked to Alnwick

Andrew Barton.alt: The wounded Scottish captain Andrew Barton directing sailors aboard his storm-battered ship during a 1511 sea battle
Andrew Barton.caption: A visual interpretation of Andrew Barton fighting the Lion to the last
Andrew Barton.pullquote: Fight on, my men, I am hurt but I am not slain.

Awd Goggie.alt: A small mossy orchard bogey rising from a gooseberry bush as a farm child pulls their hand away
Awd Goggie.caption: A visual interpretation of Awd Goggie guarding unripe fruit in a Yorkshire orchard
Awd Goggie.pullquote: Its rustling presence in the leaves was enough to keep small hands at bay.

Glaistig.alt: A grey-clad Highland Glaistig with a goat's lower body guiding a calf back toward its herd
Glaistig.caption: A visual interpretation of the protective Glaistig tending Highland cattle
Glaistig.pullquote: She could be protective — herding cattle and caring for children — or predatory.

Pendle Witches.alt: A group of accused Pendle women walking under guard across the Lancashire moor beneath Pendle Hill
Pendle Witches.caption: A visual interpretation of the accused Pendle women being taken across the Lancashire landscape
Pendle Witches.section_heading: The trial that defined English witchcraft
Pendle Witches.pullquote: The trial of the Pendle witches in 1612 is the most famous and best-documented witch case in English history.

Grace O'Malley.alt: Grace O'Malley commanding a Gaelic galley through Clew Bay with Rockfleet Castle beyond
Grace O'Malley.caption: A visual interpretation of Grace O'Malley leading her crew past Rockfleet Castle
Grace O'Malley.pullquote: The sea-captain Gráinne Ní Mháille ruled the shores of Clew Bay and negotiated with Elizabeth I as an equal.

Rhiannon.alt: Rhiannon riding a pale horse calmly along a sunlit Welsh ridge while mounted pursuers follow behind
Rhiannon.caption: A visual interpretation of Rhiannon riding calmly beyond mortal pursuit
Rhiannon.pullquote: She first appears riding calmly beyond mortal pursuit, impossible to catch unless asked to stop.

Glastonbury Tor.alt: A small boat carrying a cloaked wounded figure across flooded reeds toward Glastonbury Tor at dawn
Glastonbury Tor.caption: A visual interpretation of Glastonbury Tor as the island of Avalon
Glastonbury Tor.pullquote: An entrance to the fairy underworld is hidden in its flanks.

Sawney Bean.alt: Ragged watchers of the Sawney Bean clan crouching at a cave mouth above the Ayrshire coast as a lone rider approaches
Sawney Bean.caption: A visual interpretation of the Sawney Bean legend on the Ayrshire coast
Sawney Bean.pullquote: King James VI himself led a posse of four hundred men and bloodhounds to the cave.

Pooka.alt: A black horse with glowing eyes carrying a terrified rider through a flooded Irish bog lane at dusk
Pooka.caption: A visual interpretation of the Irish pooka in horse form
Pooka.pullquote: Sweeping up the unwary and setting them down again, shaken and far from home, by dawn.

Dick Turpin.alt: A cloaked rider on a black horse galloping along a moonlit muddy Yorkshire road past a distant coaching inn
Dick Turpin.caption: A visual interpretation of Dick Turpin haunting the old Yorkshire roads
Dick Turpin.pullquote: Turpin's ghost, or the ghost of the gallant Black Bess who died under him on that legendary ride, is said to haunt the old coaching roads, glimpsed by night where the highway runs lonely.

Gelert.alt: A great shaggy hound standing beside an overturned cradle in a torchlit medieval Welsh chamber with a dead wolf behind
Gelert.caption: A visual interpretation of Gelert in the hall at Beddgelert
Gelert.pullquote: Too late Llywelyn understood, and he is said never to have smiled again.

Lyonesse.alt: A lone rider crossing a storm-lashed stone causeway above the sea with distant half-submerged towers off Cornwall
Lyonesse.caption: A visual interpretation of the drowned land of Lyonesse
Lyonesse.map_title: Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
Lyonesse.pullquote: A drowned kingdom said to lie beneath the waves between Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly - a land of a hundred and forty churches, lost in a single night of catastrophic flooding.

Bean Nighe.alt: The Bean Nighe crouched beside a stony Highland burn washing pale grave-clothes at dusk
Bean Nighe.caption: A visual interpretation of the Highland Bean Nighe at a lonely ford
Bean Nighe.pullquote: To see her is to know that death is coming.

Boggarts.alt: A lone child pausing before a narrow stone footbridge over a dark boggy clough at dusk in northern England
Boggarts.caption: A visual interpretation of boggart-haunted country in Yorkshire and Lancashire

Brahan Seer.alt: The Brahan Seer standing on a Ross-shire shore holding a holed stone beneath a low Highland sky
Brahan Seer.caption: A visual interpretation of the Brahan Seer on the Ross-shire coast
Brahan Seer.pullquote: Long strings of carriages without horses.

Lincoln Imp.alt: The tiny horned Lincoln Imp carved high on a stone column inside the Angel Choir of Lincoln Cathedral
Lincoln Imp.caption: A visual interpretation of the Lincoln Imp in the Angel Choir
Lincoln Imp.pullquote: The angels duly did - turning the imp instantly to stone and fixing him forever in the cleft of a column high on the north side of the choir.

Spectre of Newby Church.alt: A tall hooded figure draped in a pale shroud standing beside the altar inside a small Yorkshire church
Spectre of Newby Church.caption: A visual interpretation of the Spectre of Newby Church near the altar
Spectre of Newby Church.pullquote: The image circulated for decades as apparent evidence of the supernatural.

Black Dog of Bouley Bay.alt: A huge black hound with a dragging chain on the cliff lane above Bouley Bay under storm clouds
Black Dog of Bouley Bay.caption: A visual interpretation of the Black Dog of Bouley Bay on Jersey's north coast
Black Dog of Bouley Bay.pullquote: To meet it was an omen of misfortune or of coming storm.

Ruari Mòr MacNeil of Barra.alt: Ruari Mòr MacNeil standing beside the sea at Kisimul Castle with Castlebay behind him under a low Hebridean sky
Ruari Mòr MacNeil of Barra.caption: A visual interpretation of Ruari Mòr MacNeil at Kisimul Castle
Ruari Mòr MacNeil of Barra.pullquote: Each evening his herald proclaimed that since Ruairi Mòr had dined, the kings of the earth might now eat.

Witch of Berkeley.alt: A black horse with iron hooks across its harness carrying away a shrouded woman through a moonlit Gloucestershire churchyard
Witch of Berkeley.caption: A visual interpretation of the Witch of Berkeley legend in the churchyard at night
Witch of Berkeley.pullquote: The Devil appeared on 'a black horse of immense size with iron hooks projecting over the whole of its back'.

Molly Downer.alt: Molly Downer standing outside a thatched cottage near Bembridge at winter dusk with the muddy lane falling away beside her
Molly Downer.caption: A visual interpretation of Molly Downer at Witches Hatch near Bembridge
Molly Downer.pullquote: Reputed to be the last witch of the Isle of Wight, she lived at 'Witches Hatch' near Bembridge and cursed a tormentor with fatal bad luck.

Uther Pendragon and Pendragon Castle.alt: Uther Pendragon standing beside a failed river channel below his stronghold in the rain-dark Mallerstang valley
Uther Pendragon and Pendragon Castle.caption: A visual interpretation of Uther Pendragon and the untamed River Eden
Uther Pendragon and Pendragon Castle.section_heading: Eden will run where Eden ran
Uther Pendragon and Pendragon Castle.pullquote: Let Uther Pendragon do what he can, Eden will run where Eden ran.

facts.Motif: The river that would not be tamed

Cormoran, the Giant of St Michael's Moun.alt: The giant Cormoran carrying a stolen ox across the flooded causeway below St Michael's Mount
Cormoran, the Giant of St Michael's Moun.caption: A visual interpretation of Cormoran returning to St Michael's Mount
Cormoran, the Giant of St Michael's Moun.pullquote: When his hunger stirred he would wade ashore at low tide and seize the cattle and sheep of the local farmers.

Gogmagog.alt: The giant Gogmagog wrestling Corineus at the edge of a storm-dark cliff above the sea
Gogmagog.caption: A visual interpretation of Gogmagog's legendary wrestling match with Corineus
Gogmagog.pullquote: Corineus heaved the giant onto his shoulders and hurled him from the heights to the rocks below.

William Kidd.alt: Captain William Kidd standing on the rain-wet deck of a seventeenth-century privateer off the Scottish coast
William Kidd.caption: A visual interpretation of Captain Kidd before piracy and privateering became inseparable in legend
William Kidd.pullquote: He was sent to hunt pirates and returned accused of piracy himself.

Oilliphéist.alt: The vast black-scaled Oilliphéist forcing a new river channel through rain-soaked Irish bogland
Oilliphéist.caption: A visual interpretation of the Oilliphéist carving the course of the River Shannon
Oilliphéist.section_heading: The great beast in the land
Oilliphéist.pullquote: Its enormous body writhing through the limestone carved the course of the great river as it went.

Enfield Poltergeist.alt: A wooden chair and household objects moving inexplicably in an empty 1970s north-London living room
Enfield Poltergeist.caption: A restrained visual interpretation of the reported disturbances in the Enfield house
Enfield Poltergeist.pullquote: The family described knockings, furniture that slid and overturned, and objects that flew across rooms.

Glastonbury Holy Thorn.alt: A weathered hawthorn flowering in frost on Wearyall Hill with Glastonbury Tor beyond the winter mist
Glastonbury Holy Thorn.caption: A visual interpretation of the Glastonbury Holy Thorn flowering at Christmas
Glastonbury Holy Thorn.pullquote: Joseph of Arimathea's staff took root as a hawthorn that flowers both at Christmas and in spring.

Mersey Mermaid.alt: A dark-haired mermaid watching an approaching storm from tidal rocks in the Mersey estuary
Mersey Mermaid.caption: A visual interpretation of the Mersey Mermaid as a warning from the deep
Mersey Mermaid.pullquote: The sea is beautiful and generous but never to be trusted.

Denbigh Dragon.alt: Sion y Bodiau facing the Denbigh Dragon outside the castle great hall in driving rain
Denbigh Dragon.caption: A visual interpretation of Sion y Bodiau confronting the Denbigh Dragon
Denbigh Dragon.section_heading: The dragon in the great hall
Denbigh Dragon.pullquote: He drove his broadsword into the unscaled skin at the base of the dragon's wing.

Du Sith.alt: The black-clad archer Du Sith drawing his bow above a rain-swept battlefield on Islay
Du Sith.caption: A visual interpretation of Du Sith at the Battle of Traigh Ghruinneard
Du Sith.pullquote: A sinister black-clad archer of supernatural skill decided the day from concealment.

Osmington White Horse.alt: The chalk figure of King George III on horseback cut across Osmington Hill above Weymouth Bay
Osmington White Horse.caption: A visual interpretation of the Osmington White Horse being cut into the Dorset hillside
Osmington White Horse.pullquote: The mounted figure has looked out across Weymouth Bay since 1808.

Havelok the Dane.alt: Havelok sleeping in a fisherman's house as a small golden flame rises from his mouth and Goldborough watches
Havelok the Dane.caption: A visual interpretation of Goldborough discovering Havelok's royal nature
Havelok the Dane.section_heading: The flame and the golden cross
Havelok the Dane.pullquote: At night Goldborough saw a miraculous flame issuing from her sleeping husband's mouth.

Hagg Worm.alt: A huge dark-scaled Hagg Worm coiled in a rain-soaked wooded gully on the North Yorkshire Moors
Hagg Worm.caption: A visual interpretation of the Hagg Worm in its moorland lair
Hagg Worm.pullquote: Something old and dangerous might still be coiled in the wild, sucking bogs of the haggs.

facts.Motif: The monster bound to the land

Mari Lwyd.alt: A lantern-lit Mari Lwyd party carrying a ribboned horse skull to the door of a Welsh stone cottage
Mari Lwyd.caption: A visual interpretation of the Mari Lwyd winter wassailing custom
Mari Lwyd.pullquote: The party trades verses with householders before being admitted for food, drink, and seasonal chaos.

Changeling.alt: An old farmhouse cradle holding an uncanny substitute woven from roots, moss and cloth beside an open window
Changeling.caption: A symbolic visual interpretation of the changeling belief
Changeling.pullquote: The fairies would steal a human child and leave a substitute in the cradle.

Dearg Due.alt: Dearg Due standing beside a stone-weighted grave beneath an ancient tree in misty Waterford
Dearg Due.caption: A visual interpretation of Dearg Due rising near Strongbow's Tree
Dearg Due.pullquote: On the first anniversary of her death she rose from her grave and returned as a creature of appetite and revenge.

The Henham Dragon.alt: A small winged serpent with feathered eyes rising above the bracken beside a dark Essex woodland track
The Henham Dragon.caption: A visual interpretation of the flying serpent reported at Henham in 1669
The Henham Dragon.pullquote: A nine-foot winged serpent was reported in the woods - almost certainly a hoax, but one that became a village legend.

Mary Read.alt: Mary Read gripping a cutlass and the rail of a rain-lashed pirate sloop as another vessel approaches
Mary Read.caption: A visual interpretation of Mary Read defending Rackham's sloop in 1720
Mary Read.section_heading: The last fighter on the deck
Mary Read.pullquote: It was said that Read and Bonny were the only two still defending the deck while the men hid below.

facts.Motif: A life lived across every boundary

Merlin's Oak.alt: The dead trunk of Merlin's Oak bound with iron bands beside a flooded street in Carmarthen
Merlin's Oak.caption: A visual interpretation of Merlin's Oak before its final removal
Merlin's Oak.section_heading: When the oak shall tumble down
Merlin's Oak.pullquote: When Merlin's Oak shall tumble down, then shall fall Carmarthen town.

facts.Motif: The fall of the oak and the flood

Blue Ben of Kilve.alt: The slate-blue dragon Blue Ben struggling in a collapsing section of the layered cliffs at Kilve
Blue Ben of Kilve.caption: A visual interpretation of Blue Ben falling from the fossil-rich Somerset cliffs
Blue Ben of Kilve.section_heading: The blue dragon in the cliffs
Blue Ben of Kilve.pullquote: When it fell into the sea, fossil bones in the cliffs were pointed to as proof of the beast.

Morgawrr.alt: A long-necked humped sea creature surfacing beside a small fishing boat in stormy Falmouth Bay
Morgawrr.caption: A visual interpretation of Morgawrr surfacing in Falmouth Bay
Morgawrr.pullquote: Witnesses describe a humped creature fifteen to twenty feet long, raising a small head on a long neck from the swell.

Bran the Blessed.alt: The giant king Bran the Blessed wading through the Irish Sea while carrying warriors and musicians
Bran the Blessed.caption: A visual interpretation of Bran carrying his host across the Irish Sea
Bran the Blessed.map_title: Britain, Ireland and the White Hill
Bran the Blessed.section_heading: The king no house could contain
Bran the Blessed.pullquote: He waded the Irish Sea at the head of his host, his musicians playing on his back.

Owlman of Mawnan.alt: A tall owl-headed humanoid with separate arms and folded wings standing on Mawnan church tower at twilight
Owlman of Mawnan.caption: A visual interpretation of the humanoid Owlman reported at Mawnan in 1976
Owlman of Mawnan.pullquote: Witnesses described a huge owl-like humanoid with red eyes and black pincer-like claws.

Piskie.alt: A small ragged Piskie beckoning toward a misleading light beside a foggy path on Bodmin Moor
Piskie.caption: A visual interpretation of a traveller being piskie-led on the West Country moors
Piskie.pullquote: To be piskie-led is to wander in circles while the familiar world quietly rearranges itself.

Pixie.alt: Three small ragged pixies secretly riding and braiding the mane of a dark pony in a Devon stable
Pixie.caption: A visual interpretation of West Country pixies at their night mischief
Pixie.pullquote: They steal horses to ride through the night, returning them exhausted and sweated by dawn.

Corineus.alt: The Trojan hero Corineus lifting the giant Gogmagog across his shoulders beside a storm-dark Cornish cliff
Corineus.caption: A visual interpretation of Corineus overcoming Gogmagog at the cliff edge
Corineus.pullquote: Having had three ribs broken, he heaved the giant up and hurled him from the heights.

Ragnar Lothbrok.alt: Ragnar Lothbrok standing defiantly among snakes in a rain-dark stone pit at York
Ragnar Lothbrok.caption: A visual interpretation of Ragnar singing his final death-song in King Ælla's snake pit
Ragnar Lothbrok.section_heading: The old boar in the snake pit
Ragnar Lothbrok.pullquote: He sang as he died and warned that the little pigs would grunt if they knew what the old boar suffered.

Salmon of Knowledge.alt: A great silver salmon swallowing fallen hazelnuts beneath ancient trees in the clear Well of Segais
Salmon of Knowledge.caption: A visual interpretation of the Salmon of Knowledge at the source of the Boyne
Salmon of Knowledge.section_heading: The fish that ate all wisdom
Salmon of Knowledge.pullquote: The hazelnuts fell into the water and were eaten by the salmon, infusing it with all the knowledge in the world.

facts.Setting: Well of Segais and River Boyne

Thanet Sea Monster.alt: Three sailors watch a huge dark sea creature surface in rough water off the chalk cliffs of Thanet
Thanet Sea Monster.caption: A visual interpretation of the 1917 sea-monster report off the Isle of Thanet
Thanet Sea Monster.pullquote: The sailors opened fire; at least one shot struck the dorsal fin, causing the creature to thrash violently before sinking beneath the surface.

Janet Forsyth, the Westray Storm Witch.alt: Janet Forsyth grips the tiller of a storm-battered sailing vessel approaching the low shore of Westray
Janet Forsyth, the Westray Storm Witch.caption: A visual interpretation of Janet Forsyth guiding a vessel into Pierowall Bay
Janet Forsyth, the Westray Storm Witch.pullquote: The gap between this romantic rescue story and the grim trial record makes Janet Forsyth one of the most poignant examples of how Orkney folk memory reshaped a real execution into legend.

Bures Dragon.alt: Villagers with longbows confront a crested dragon beside the River Stour marsh near Bures
Bures Dragon.caption: A visual interpretation of the dragon encounter recorded near Bures in 1405
Bures Dragon.pullquote: Local men attempted to kill the beast with arrows, but the shafts rebounded harmlessly off its scales.

Gog and Magog.alt: Two giant wickerwork effigies of Gog and Magog carried through a crowded medieval London street
Gog and Magog.caption: A visual interpretation of Gog and Magog in the medieval Lord Mayor's Show
Gog and Magog.pullquote: The wickerwork and wooden giants have been destroyed and remade many times — lost in the Great Fire, shattered in the Blitz — and always restored, for the city regards them as its protectors.

Tylwyth Teg.alt: Pale-clothed dancers form a fairy ring beside a moonlit Welsh lake as a traveller watches from a stone wall
Tylwyth Teg.caption: A visual interpretation of the Fair Family dancing in the Welsh hills
Tylwyth Teg.map_title: The hills and lakes of mid Wales
Tylwyth Teg.section_heading: A night in the fairy ring
Tylwyth Teg.pullquote: A mortal drawn into their ring to dance might find, on stepping out, that a single night had been a hundred years.

Rheidol.alt: A young woman personifying the Rheidol runs beside a mountain stream descending from Plynlimon toward Cardigan Bay
Rheidol.caption: A visual interpretation of Rheidol racing from Plynlimon to the sea
Rheidol.pullquote: She flung herself straight west down the mountainside, carving a steep and narrow valley through rock and forest, and reached Cardigan Bay at the place now called Aberystwyth before either of her sisters had even cleared the foothills.

The Selkie.alt: A Donegal selkie woman carries her recovered dark seal skin toward the Atlantic as a fisherman watches from a stone croft
The Selkie.caption: A visual interpretation of the selkie wife's return to the sea
The Selkie.pullquote: When she eventually finds the hidden skin, she puts it on at once, walks into the waves without hesitation, and does not look back at husband or children.

Tintagel.alt: Tintagel's ruined castle rises above Merlin's Cave as a lone cloaked figure stands at the low-tide entrance
Tintagel.caption: A visual interpretation of Merlin's Cave beneath the Tintagel headland
Tintagel.pullquote: Whether or not any historical Arthur ever trod the headland, Tintagel remains the single place most powerfully bound to his legend, where landscape, ruin and story meet above the Cornish sea.

Westbury White Horse.alt: A white horse walks beside a moonlit spring below the Westbury White Horse chalk figure and Bratton church
Westbury White Horse.caption: A visual interpretation of the Westbury horse descending to drink at midnight
Westbury White Horse.section_heading: The horse that walks at midnight
Westbury White Horse.pullquote: Wiltshire folklore holds that when the church clock at Bratton strikes midnight, the horse descends the steep hillside to drink from the Briddle Springs at its foot.

Long Compton Witches.alt: An elderly woman walks alone along a muddy Victorian village lane while Long Compton neighbours watch from a distance
Long Compton Witches.caption: A visual interpretation of the climate of witch-belief in Long Compton in 1875
Long Compton Witches.map_title: Long Compton and the Rollright Hills
Long Compton Witches.section_heading: The belief that outlived the trials
Long Compton Witches.pullquote: It represents a rare case where rural witch-belief survived in documented form into the Victorian period with a specific named victim, a named killer, and a court record.

Brown Man of the Muirs.alt: A bracken-clad moor guardian warns a seated hunter beside a spring on the Northumberland moors
Brown Man of the Muirs.caption: A visual interpretation of the Brown Man confronting hunters on the Border moors
Brown Man of the Muirs.pullquote: The Brown Man stands among the oldest expressions of a folk idea that the wilderness has its own keeper, who exacts a price from those who abuse it.

Petticoat Loose.alt: A solitary woman kneels beside moonlit Bay Lough trying to twist a crumbling rope from wet sand
Petticoat Loose.caption: A visual interpretation of Petticoat Loose's endless task at Bay Lough
Petticoat Loose.section_heading: The rope that can never hold
Petticoat Loose.pullquote: Condemned to an impossible, endless task: to twist ropes of sand, or empty the lough with a thimble, so that she can never finish and return.

Marool.alt: A many-eyed dark sea creature surfaces in glowing mareel near a small Shetland fishing boat during a gale
Marool.caption: A visual interpretation of the Marool moving through Shetland's phosphorescent sea
Marool.pullquote: Where the islanders saw that eerie green-blue luminescence, they might fear the presence of the Marool beneath.

Stronsay Beast.alt: Orkney islanders measure and sketch an enormous decayed sea-creature carcass on the rocky shore of Stronsay in 1808
Stronsay Beast.caption: A visual interpretation of the 1808 examination of the Stronsay Beast
Stronsay Beast.pullquote: Yet the Stronsay Beast endures in Orkney lore as the islands' own sea-monster — a vivid moment where folklore, natural history and the romance of the unknown all washed up together on a northern shore.

Macha.alt: The pregnant goddess Macha races two dark horses below the royal earthworks of Emain Macha
Macha.caption: A visual interpretation of Macha's coerced race against the horses of Ulster
Macha.pullquote: She begged for delay until the child was born; the king refused.

Crom Cruach.alt: Adult worshippers bow around a gold-covered central idol and twelve lesser stones on the rain-dark Plain of Prostrations
Crom Cruach.caption: A visual reconstruction of the Crom Cruach tradition at Magh Slécht
Crom Cruach.pullquote: In 1921, a broken, cone-shaped stone covered in spiralling Iron Age La Tène carvings was unearthed at Killycluggin, close to Magh Slécht.

Donn.alt: Donn stands beside the sea tunnel through storm-dark Bull Rock as wreckage pitches in the Atlantic below
Donn.caption: A visual interpretation of Donn reaching Tech Duinn, the House of the Dead
Donn.section_heading: The house in the western sea
Donn.pullquote: To me, to my house, you shall all come after your deaths.

Njuggle.alt: A Shetland blacksmith fits an iron shoe to a wet grey pony with a wheel-curled tail beside an old watermill
Njuggle.caption: A visual interpretation of the blacksmith breaking the njuggle's power with iron
Njuggle.pullquote: Iron, in the Scottish and Norse supernatural tradition, is proof against magical creatures, and once the shoes were nailed on, the njuggle lost its power entirely.

Nuada of the Silver Hand.alt: The healer Dian Cecht fits a jointed silver right arm to the seated king Nuada in a misty early Irish encampment
Nuada of the Silver Hand.caption: A visual interpretation of Nuada receiving the silver arm that restored his kingship
Nuada of the Silver Hand.section_heading: The arm that restored a king
Nuada of the Silver Hand.pullquote: The healer-god Dian Cecht fashioned him a silver arm that moved like a real one, restoring his wholeness and his right to reign.

facts.Type: King of the Tuatha Dé Danann

Gearóid Iarla of Lough Gur.alt: Gearóid Iarla rides a white horse with silver shoes across the moonlit surface of Lough Gur
Gearóid Iarla of Lough Gur.caption: A visual interpretation of Gearóid Iarla's seven-year ride across Lough Gur
Gearóid Iarla of Lough Gur.pullquote: Every seven years, when conditions are right, he rides out across the surface of the horseshoe-shaped lake on a white horse whose hooves are shod in silver.

Trow.alt: A Shetland fiddler listens outside a snowy burial mound while short grey-clad trows feast and play music within
Trow.caption: A visual interpretation of a human fiddler learning music from the trows beneath a mound
Trow.pullquote: They were famous for stealing fiddle-tunes, and many a Shetland reel was said to have been learned by a human fiddler who overheard the trows playing in their mound.

Gurt Worm.alt: A Somerset woodman discovers that the mossy log beneath his bread and cheese is a huge serpent in Shervage Wood
Gurt Worm.caption: A visual interpretation of the woodman's encounter with the Gurt Worm
Gurt Worm.pullquote: Rather than flee, the unflappable countryman set about the worm with his axe, cutting it in two.

Jinny the Witch (Joney Lowney).alt: Joney Lowney stands in a sackcloth penitential garment beside a stone market cross as Manx villagers watch
Jinny the Witch (Joney Lowney).caption: A visual interpretation of Joney Lowney's public penance on the Isle of Man
Jinny the Witch (Joney Lowney).section_heading: From court record to festival song
Jinny the Witch (Joney Lowney).pullquote: In that form she became permanently attached to Hop tu Naa, the Manx Celtic New Year festival held on 31 October.

Loch na Beiste Water Horse, Mellon Udrig.alt: Nineteenth-century Highland workers cut a drainage channel and pour quicklime beside Loch na Beiste as a dark keel-shaped form moves offshore
Loch na Beiste Water Horse, Mellon Udrig.caption: A visual interpretation of the attempt to drain Loch na Beiste in the 1840s
Loch na Beiste Water Horse, Mellon Udrig.section_heading: The loch they tried to drain
Loch na Beiste Water Horse, Mellon Udrig.pullquote: The creature, needless to say, was never found, and the loch defeated its would-be exterminators.

Waun Mawn.alt: A Neolithic community uses ropes and timber levers to lower a bluestone from the Waun Mawn circle at dawn
Waun Mawn.caption: A visual reconstruction of the dismantling of the Waun Mawn stone circle
Waun Mawn.pullquote: The evidence suggests that Neolithic communities dismantled their great Welsh circle and dragged its stones 150 miles eastward to Wiltshire, carrying not just stone but the cultural memory of their monument.

Ynys Enlli.alt: A medieval pilgrim boat crosses rough Bardsey Sound toward the mist-covered slopes and monastery of Ynys Enlli
Ynys Enlli.caption: A visual interpretation of the pilgrim crossing to Ynys Enlli
Ynys Enlli.pullquote: Whether as a saints' graveyard, Merlin's resting place, or Arthur's Avalon, Ynys Enlli's isolation and the danger of crossing its sound have long given the island an otherworldly reputation.

Long Man of Wilmington.alt: An early eighteenth-century antiquarian sketches the enormous white outline of the Long Man on Windover Hill
Long Man of Wilmington.caption: A visual interpretation of the Long Man around the time of its earliest surviving record
Long Man of Wilmington.pullquote: Its age and meaning are genuine mysteries.

Zennor.alt: The carved medieval mermaid bench-end inside St Senara Church at Zennor in soft Cornish daylight
Zennor.caption: A visual interpretation of the mermaid bench-end at St Senara Church, Zennor
Zennor.pullquote: Ships in the cove are said to sometimes hear Trewhella's voice rising from the water, still singing.

Wayland the Smith.alt: Wayland's Smithy at dawn with an unshod horse waiting beside the Neolithic barrow on the Ridgeway
Wayland the Smith.caption: A visual interpretation of Wayland the Smith at Wayland's Smithy on the Ridgeway
Wayland the Smith.pullquote: Tradition — already old when the Saxons named the place — held that a traveller whose horse had cast a shoe need only leave the beast there with a coin overnight, and by morning the unseen smith would have shod it.

Old Man of Storr.alt: The black basalt pinnacle of the Old Man of Storr rising above wet grass on Skye with sea beyond
Old Man of Storr.caption: A visual interpretation of the Old Man of Storr on the Trotternish Ridge
Old Man of Storr.pullquote: When the giant died and was buried in the hillside, his thumb was left protruding above the ground — and there it has stood ever since, weathering into the jagged spire seen today.

Fachan.alt: The one-eyed, one-legged Fachan crossing a rain-dark track in Glen Etive beneath heavy Highland cloud
Fachan.caption: A visual interpretation of the Fachan in Glen Etive
Fachan.section_heading: The straight one of Glen Etive
Fachan.pullquote: It is a being of terrible single-ness: one eye in the middle of its face, one hand reaching from its chest, one leg beneath it, and a single tuft of dark feathers or hair on its head.

Cu Sith.alt: The shaggy green Cu Sith crossing a wet Skye moor at dusk with its tail curled high above the heather
Cu Sith.caption: A visual interpretation of the Cu Sith on the moors of Skye
Cu Sith.pullquote: Those bays were a death-warning: anyone who heard them and failed to reach safety before the third was said to be overcome, or carried off.

Dando's Dogs.alt: A dark rider and pack of hounds driving along a storm-struck Cornish track at dusk
Dando's Dogs.caption: A visual interpretation of Dando's spectral hunt in Cornwall
Dando's Dogs.pullquote: Ever since, the country folk said, Dando and his dogs may be heard on stormy nights sweeping across the Cornish sky and moors in a spectral hunt, the baying of the hounds carrying on the wind.

Beltane Fire Festival.alt: Torch-bearing Beltane participants and drummers processing across Calton Hill above Edinburgh at night
Beltane Fire Festival.caption: A visual interpretation of the modern Beltane procession on Calton Hill
Beltane Fire Festival.pullquote: Though a contemporary creation rather than an unbroken survival, it consciously revives the imagery and meaning of the old Beltane.

Duergar.alt: A lone traveller on the Simonside Hills approaching a false lantern light near a crouching Duergar at the cliff edge
Duergar.caption: A visual interpretation of the Duergar luring a traveller on the Simonside Hills
Duergar.pullquote: The Simonside Hills kept their reputation as a place no wise man crossed after dark.

Finfolk.alt: Two dark Finfolk sea-sorcerers in a narrow boat off a rocky Orkney shore at dusk
Finfolk.caption: A visual interpretation of Finfolk nearing the Orkney shore
Finfolk.pullquote: They steal mortals for spouses and servants.

Tom Hickathrift.alt: Tom Hickathrift facing the giant of the Marshland with a cart wheel and axle on a muddy Fenland causeway
Tom Hickathrift.caption: A visual interpretation of Tom Hickathrift fighting the giant of the Marshland
Tom Hickathrift.section_heading: The giant on the marsh road
Tom Hickathrift.pullquote: Tom upended his cart, took the axle for a club and a wheel for a shield, and beat the giant to death, winning his hoard and his land for the people.

Mary Butters, the Carnmoney Witch.alt: Mary Butters tending a smoking pot of milk and nails inside a dark County Antrim farmhouse while a man stands watch outside the door
Mary Butters, the Carnmoney Witch.caption: A visual interpretation of Mary Butters performing the Carnmoney bewitchment cure
Mary Butters, the Carnmoney Witch.section_heading: The night of the smoke cure
Mary Butters, the Carnmoney Witch.pullquote: She sealed a farmhouse in foul smoke to perform her rite and two people were found dead by dawn.

Bardney Abbey and the Light of Oswald.alt: Monks at Bardney Abbey watching a pale pillar of light rise from King Oswald's bier outside the timber gate at night
Bardney Abbey and the Light of Oswald.caption: A visual interpretation of the miracle at Bardney Abbey
Bardney Abbey and the Light of Oswald.pullquote: During the night, according to Bede, a pillar of light rose from the body of Oswald and blazed upward into the sky, visible across all the surrounding countryside.
